review_notes: I read the whole target file and the relevant parts of Coinduced/Functor.lean (coindFunctor definition, coindFunctor_obj, coindFunctor_map_apply and its impl lemma). I also read the simp lemmas coind_incl_apply and coind_proj_apply in Exact.lean. The only simp-interface weakness I found is that coindFunctor's simp lemma on maps is stated pointwise with eqToHom transports. It cannot fire on the bare `((coindFunctor R G U).map f).hom.hom` that the theorems in this file mention, so the file falls back on repeated `change`s. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether the proposed bare-map equation can be proved by `rfl` or can be stated with simp-friendly typing. The `change` steps compile at default transparency, which suggests it can, but I have not tested that.

findings.problem: The only simp lemma for the underlying map of `(coindFunctor R G U).map f` is `coindFunctor_map_apply`. It is stated pointwise and wrapped in `eqToHom` transports and a `show … from`. It therefore does not match the bare `((coindFunctor R G U).map f).hom.hom` that appears in the statements. Consumers must instead use a defeq `change` to expose `DiscreteCoind.map` (lines 96, 101, 103, 116). Each `change` restates the long `DiscreteCoind.map f'.toLinearMap (DiscreteRep.equivariant f')` term, where `f'` is `(ofSmoothDiscrete R U).map f`. The proofs also need the auxiliary equalities `hi` and `hp`, which are re-proved by hand from `coind_incl_apply` and `coind_proj_apply`. Normalising `coindFunctor.map` to `DiscreteCoind.map` is not available to `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: In Coinduced/Functor.lean, next to `coindFunctor_map_apply`, add a simp-normal-form lemma that rewrites the bare underlying map of `(coindFunctor R G U).map f` to `DiscreteCoind.map ((ofSmoothDiscrete R U).map f).toLinearMap (DiscreteRep.equivariant _)`. It can be proved by `rfl`, since the `change`s here already rely on that definitional equality. If this cannot be stated without `eqToHom` transports because of the object-level cast, state it as a `Function.Injective`/`Surjective`/`Exact` transport lemma. Then replace the `change` steps by `simp only [thatLemma]` or `rw`. The `hi`/`hp` rewriting could then also go through the existing simp lemmas `coind_incl_apply` and `coind_proj_apply`.
findings.benefit: The proofs would no longer restate the long `DiscreteCoind.map` terms and would not depend on `change` unfolding the composite functor. Any other file that works with `(coindFunctor R G U).map f` would get the same canonical form from `simp`. The `coindFunctor` simp interface would then be complete: the object case already has `coindFunctor_obj`, but the map case does not.
